transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2028-01-17
Start: 15:02 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Lodestar Head Partnerships), Leah (Infra Lead), Omar (Security), Rina (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Lodestar is exploring a channel partnership to offer GPU-accelerated inference as a managed add-on to their existing SaaS stack. Main concerns: integration model (hosted vs dedicated vs VPC), pricing split, security controls (SOC2, KMS), and performance SLAs. Redwood AE/SE provided high-level runtime and orchestration overview, suggested a short benchmark POC and reciprocal docs exchange.

Topics:
- Partner motion and commercial structure
- Technical integration patterns (API vs Peering vs On-prem connector)
- Security/compliance checklist and KMS/SSO expectations
- Pilot scope: perf benchmarks, telemetry, and billing integration

Action items (covered in metadata)

Transcript body (timestamps approximate, transcription contains typical ASR errors, occasional mis-attributions):

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um — quick intros, uh I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on partner motions. Priya is our se, she'll go deep on perf.
[00:12] Marco: Marco here, head of partnerships at Lodestar, thanks. Leah and Omar from infra and security, and Rina on product.
[00:21] Priya: Hi all. Quick agenda: framing partner play, integration patterns, then dive into sample workload and next steps, ok?
[00:30] Marco: Sounds good. High level — Lodestar sells a white-labeled document-automation saas to legal and finance teams. We're seeing demand for LLM features but customers ask about latency and data residency, so we want an offering we can bundle and resell with a partner who can do GPU hosting and predictable SLAs.
[00:48] Alex: Great, that's the exact motion Redwood targets. Two quick Qs — timeline for launch and what counts as success?
[00:57] Marco: We'd like a pilot in Q1, production by end of Q2. Success is sub-500ms 95th pct for our short chat flows, and cost per active user under $0.20/month in the model piece — that's an internal target, flexible though.
[01:20] Leah: For infra, our infra constraints: we run in three regions, prefer peering or VPC-to-VPC rather than public egress for compliance. We also want per-tenant isolation for enterprise customers.
[01:36] Omar: Security side — SOC2 Type II in the roadmap, must have SAML/SSO, audit logs, and KMS integration for customer keys (HSM optional). Data retention needs to be configurable per customer, and we may need an on-prem option for one customer.
[01:55] Priya: OK noted. From a technical pattern point, we usually propose three options: 1) Hosted API model — fastest to ship, Redwood hosts models, we provide tenancy segregation at the API layer; 2) Dedicated pools for reserved GPU capacity with predictable throughput and private networking; 3) Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) where control plane runs separately — heavier ops but meets strict residency and key control.
[02:28] Marco: What's the tradeoff on latency and cost between those?
[02:32] Priya: Hosted is lowest friction but cost per token can be higher at scale; we can do caching and batching to reduce cost but it impacts tail latency. Dedicated pools give better unit economics and predictable latency because you control GPU allocation. Private deployments remove cross-tenant risk and let you integrate KMS/HSM but onboarding takes more time.
[02:53] Leah: Regarding VPC, do you support VPC peering or do we need a transit? Our infra uses VPC peering with route tables.
[02:59] Alex: We support VPC peering and private link style peering, yes. For Dedicated we can peer into a customer's VPC and provide internal endpoints. For private on-prem we do a customer-managed control plane and can run inference nodes behind their NICs.
[03:16] Omar: On keys — can Redwood use our customer-managed KMS or you require Redwood KMS? Also, HSM for certain enterprise customers?
[03:23] Priya: We have integrations for customer KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and can support HSM-backed keys where needed. That said, some internal telemetry may still go to Redwood's control plane, we can minimize what we store and encrypt in flight. We'll send a pen-test and network diagram after NDA.
[03:45] Marco: Cool. On the commercial side, do you do revenue share or simple resale with partner uplift?
[03:50] Alex: We do both; early partnerships usually start with a rebate/whitelabel comms piece and then migrate to a revenue share when there's volume. We'll share a partner one-pager.
[03:59] Rina: For the product fit — our customers run two main flows: 1) short Q&A (avg 20 tokens per turn, bursts of 1k reqs/min during business hrs) and 2) document summarization with longer contexts (avg 2k tokens input). We need structured output and function calling style so the client can parse.
[04:22] Priya: That helps. For short Q&A, we can recommend a smaller, faster model variant with prefix caching to hit your 500ms target. For summarization, batch processing with async job queues is a better fit. We'll need a representative token distribution to size pools.
[04:42] Marco: We'll share a token distribution CSV. For the summit customers that demand data never leaves the region — is regional isolation possible?
[04:51] Alex: Yes — regional clusters and model routing by region is supported. We can also pin model versions regionally.
[04:58] Leah: Any built-in telemetry/observability we can wire into our dashboards?
[05:03] Priya: Console exposes per-route latency, token costs, traces, and you can stream traces to your observability stack. There's a webhook option and a metrics exporter for Prometheus.
[05:14] Omar: Quick nit — how do you guarantee logs aren't storing PII? We need redaction or opt-out.
[05:20] Priya: We support configurable retention, and a redaction pipeline on ingestion; for strict cases we can disable ingestion to Redwood's control plane and keep logs on-prem.
[05:31] Marco: Let's talk about the pilot. We want Redwood to run a small benchmark with our typical load and then a joint POC. What would you need to run a 48-72 hour perf run?
[05:42] Priya: Sample payloads, token dist, target SLA metrics, and preferred regions. Also, a staging API key and a network route. We'll provide a runbook and script. We usually measure 95th and 99th pct latencies, p50, token cost, and throughput.
[06:01] Leah: We'll provide the payloads and a CSV. On networking, we prefer VPC peering for the test. Is that possible for a limited window?
[06:08] Alex: Yes, we can do short-lived peering for the test or set up a secure tunnel.
[06:12] Rina: On model fidelity — we need to ensure no hallucination for contract extractions. Is there an eval framework?
[06:19] Priya: We have an eval suite that runs prompt-based tests and can score hallucination/reliability against a labeled set. We can run that as part of the POC and tie alerts to regression thresholds.
[06:30] Marco: Any gotchas with KV cache or memory with long context for summarization?
[06:34] Priya: The runtime manages KV cache for attention; long contexts are handled but require more memory-per-request. For summarization workflows we recommend chunking + streaming responses. Also quantization can reduce memory but might affect quality, we'll test that.
[06:50] Omar: A question about multi-tenant isolation — if we do dedicated pools for Lodestar's customers, can we still get per-tenant billing and logs?
[06:57] Alex: Yes, we support token-level billing per tenant, route tags, and access policies. You can have role-based access and SSO integration, plus per-tenant audit logs.
[07:10] Speaker 6: [crosstalk]
[07:12] Marco: Sorry, go ahead.
[07:14] Priya: One more technical note — we also provide autoscaling policies that are workload-aware. For bursty Q&A flows you can set burst capacity, and for summarization we recommend scheduled scaling.
[07:28] Leah: How long does private deployment onboarding usually take?
[07:32] Alex: On average 6-10 weeks for a private VPC deployment with the control plane separated; on-prem can be 8-16 weeks depending on appliance and network constraints. Dedicated pools as a service are faster — typically 2-4 weeks once contracts are signed.
[07:46] Rina: For commercial, what's the minimum committed spend?
[07:50] Alex: We have flexible options; for dedicated pools there's usually a monthly commit to guarantee capacity. We'll share a few templated commit tiers. For channel partnerships we can discuss co-selling incentives instead of strict commit for early pilots.
[07:58] Marco: Competitors keep pushing lower rates; how does Redwood differentiate on perf/ops?
[08:03] Priya: We focus on predictable inference economics — intelligent batching, KV/prefix caching, model quantization recommendations, and an observable console so you can tie cost to features. Also, the unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private means less engineering lift for you.
[08:17] Omar: For compliance we'll need a SOC2 report and a diagram of data flows. Also SAML metadata for SSO.
[08:24] Alex: We'll push SOC2 docs and a network diagram after the NDA. We'll also include SSO integration docs.
[08:30] Marco: Sounds like we're aligned. A couple of edge cases: one enterprise customer requires air-gapped deploy, is that supported?
[08:37] Priya: Yes, for air-gap we do an on-prem package that runs without outbound calls; that requires more ops but is possible. We'll outline prerequisites.
[08:46] Leah: Monitoring during POC — we need export of traces to our splunk instance and token-level billing sample so we can reconcile costs.
[08:55] Priya: Splunk export is supported via HTTP event collector or a forwarder. We'll provide sample billing CSV format.
[09:03] Marco: Ok, next steps to recap?
[09:06] Alex: We'll do a quick recap, yeah. Priya will own the benchmark runbook and run the 48h test. Alex will share partner commercial framework and initial MOU. Lodestar will provide token distribution, payloads, and security questionnaire. Redwood will share SOC2 and SSO/KMS docs.
[09:24] Marco: Great. Can we schedule the POC scoping for next Tuesday?
[09:28] Alex: Tuesday works for us. We'll send a calendar invite.
[09:31] Rina: One tiny thing — can you include an example of the CLI commands for starting a dedicated pool and the API call for function calling? Those are helpful for product engineers.
[09:40] Priya: Absolutely, we'll add them to the runbook and include sample curl and SDK snippets.
[09:46] Omar: Also, please explicitly call out what telemetry Redwood will and will not retain during private deployments.
[09:52] Priya: We'll document retention defaults and opt-outs.
[09:55] Alex: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and action items.
[09:59] Marco: Thank you, great session.

End of Transcript.
